passage.label: Al-Fatiha — the complete surah read as one passage

arabicExcerpts.text: صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ غَيۡرِ ٱلۡمَغۡضُوبِ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ

mainSubject.label: Praise of Allah, exclusive worship and dependence on Him, and the plea for guidance to the straight path
mainSubject.notes: Each element of the composite subject is stated in the cited verses: al-hamd (1:2), na'budu/nasta'in (1:5), ihdina (1:6).

subordinateSubjects.label: Beginning in the name of Allah (basmala)
subordinateSubjects.notes: The basmala is counted as verse 1:1 in the pinned corpus numbering.

subordinateSubjects.label: Allah's lordship over all worlds (rabb al-'alamin)
The paired divine names ar-Rahman and ar-Rahim
Sovereignty of the Day of Recompense (malik yawm ad-din)
Worship and seeking help directed to Allah alone
The taught plea for guidance to the straight path
The path of the favored, distinguished from those who earned anger and those astray
subordinateSubjects.notes: The verse states the distinction but does not name the groups. Identification is a tafsir question and is not asserted here.

commandsAndProhibitions.description: The Qur'an teaches the supplication 'Guide us to the straight path', continued in 1:7 with the path of those upon whom Allah bestowed favor.

divineNamesAndAttributes.gloss: Lord, nurturer — here of all worlds (editorial gloss)
The Entirely Merciful — divine name (editorial gloss)
The Especially Merciful — divine name (editorial gloss)
Sovereign/Master — of the Day of Recompense (editorial gloss)

humanConditionsAndSpiritualStates.label: Grateful praise as the servant's stance before Allah
Humanity distinguished by response to guidance: favored, anger-earned, astray

relationships.label: Allah as Lord (Rabb) of all worlds — the Creator–creation relationship
Servants direct worship and requests for help to Allah alone
Guidance as a divine gift requested by the servant
Divine favor (in'am) bestowed upon a group of people

notes: Pilot record for MFD-11 Pass A. All subjects are grounded in the passage text. Identification of the groups in 1:7 (e.g., as prophets or specific communities) is a tafsir question requiring verified evidence and is deliberately not asserted. Basmala numbering follows the pinned corpus (counted as 1:1). No prophetic narrative or social/economic subject is stated in this passage, so those arrays are omitted rather than populated by inference.
